To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 4.0-kb DNA fragment in the 5'-flank region of the human DB H gene is essential to the tissue-specific expression in the central and peripheral nervous systems, and that it is also capable of ectopically promoting gene expression in some DB H -immunonegative neurons in the olfactory system.

the human DBH promoter directs neuron subtype-specific gene activity in the central nervous systems of transgenic mice, and that the 4.0-kb 5'flanking region of human DBH is sufficient to direct the neuron subtype-specific gene activation in the CNS of transgenic mice.

the human dopamine beta hydroxylase gene promoter is able to drive the human phenylethylenamine N-methyl transferase gene in the norepinephrineric and epinephrineric neurons in brain, and in the adrenal gland of transgenic mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the regulatory elements of the DBH 5'-flankinig region that are involved in the tissue- and neuron subtype-specific expression of the human DB
the development of a new animal model for studying the function and pathogenesis of catecholaminergic neurons in the brain and the adrenal gland.
the identification of cis-acting elements that regulate the tissue-specific expression in the brain and peripheral tissues, and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human DBH promoter is able to promote neuron subtype-specific gene transcription.

the DBH promoter is sufficient for neuron subtype-specific expression in the central and peripheral nervous system of transgenc mice, but not sufficient to restrict the expression of the DB H gene to the catecholaminergic neurons in the central nervous systems.

the 4 kb of the DBH 5'-flank region is essential for neuron subtype-specific expression in the central and peripheral nervous systems, but is not sufficient to confer the neuron subtype specificity of gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 4.0-kb 5' flanking sequence is sufficient for the neuron subtype-specific gene regulation of the human DBh gene in transgenic mice, but not for the complete regulation of the human PNmt gene.
the 4 kb of the 5'-flank of the human DB H gene promoter is sufficient for tissue- and cell type-specific expression of the PNMT gene in transgenic mice.
a 4-kb fragment of the DBH 5'-flaking region contains all of the information necessary to direct the neuron subtype-specific expression of the PNMT cDNA in the brain of transgenic mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5'-flank of the DBH promoter can be used to drive expression of a transgene in a subset of catecholaminergic neurons in the central nervous systems of transgenic mice.
the 4.0-kb 5' flanking region is essential to the tissue-specific expression and that it also has the potential to promote the neuron-specific expression in the CNS of transgenic mice.
we have created the transgenic mice that can express human PNMT, which is a useful model to study the role of norepinephrines in the brain.
